pages.intent: A new player wants one clear starting route through the settlement and first dungeon expedition.
pages.acceptance: The first screen identifies Dungeon Settlers, states the Early Access boundary, presents a real first-expedition planner action, and links to the Beginner, Clay, and Research pages with real content and sources.

pages.intent: A first-time player wants to understand what to prepare in the settlement before committing a party to the dungeon.
pages.acceptance: The page gives a direct first-route answer, separates official facts from cautious guidance, covers settlement needs, party size, research, expedition preparation, version limits, and links to both task guides.
requiredSections: When to return and what can change

pages.primaryKeyword: How to get clay in Dungeon Settlers
pages.intent: A player is blocked by early Clay costs and wants the current enemy, merchant, and deeper-region routes.
pages.acceptance: The page answers the Clay question before background, cites the current secondary report, labels quantities and floors as version-sensitive, explains early versus later routes, and links to the beginner and research guides.

pages.primaryKeyword: How to research in Dungeon Settlers
pages.intent: A player wants to understand what Research unlocks without trusting an unverified or outdated tech order.
pages.acceptance: The page states what the official store confirms, gives a conservative early decision method, marks unverified research-tree details as pending, and links to the beginner and Clay guides.
requiredSections: What Research is confirmed to do
How it fits the expedition loop

pages.intent: A new player wants to turn the settlement, party, Research question, and return observation into a repeatable first-run checklist.
pages.acceptance: The tool accepts a run purpose and four visible preparation checks, returns either missing items or an ordered plan, links to the matching guide, and clearly states that hidden values and best orders remain unverified.

pages.intent: A returning player wants to filter the currently published guides by the settlement or expedition problem they need to solve.
pages.acceptance: The library explains its dated evidence boundary, exposes every current guide as a real searchable entry, and offers a route into the first-expedition planner and update record.

pages.intent: A player wants to see which guide conclusions are dated and which routes should be rechecked after an Early Access change.
pages.acceptance: The update page records the current guide revision, names the affected routes, links back to the planner and guide library, and explains what remains pending rather than inventing a changelog.
